title: Group Consecutive IDs
learning_objective: Learn the id minus row_number trick for consecutive groups.

tutorial.explanation: For consecutive ids, id - row_number stays constant inside a continuous run. That constant can be used as a group key.
tutorial.syntax: WITH numbered AS (SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id) AS rn FROM stadium) SELECT id, id - rn AS group_key FROM numbered;
tutorial.mental_model: If ids are consecutive, both id and rn increase by 1 together, so their difference does not change.

guided_example.prompt: Compute a group key for consecutive ids.
guided_example.solution_query: WITH numbered AS (SELECT id, visit_date, people, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id) AS rn FROM stadium) SELECT id, id - rn AS group_key FROM numbered;
guided_example.explanation: Rows 2, 3, and 4 get the same group key because they are consecutive.

practice.prompt: Return group_key and count of rows in each consecutive group.
practice.expected_query: WITH numbered AS (SELECT id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id) AS rn FROM stadium) SELECT id - rn AS group_key, COUNT(*) AS rows_in_group FROM numbered GROUP BY id - rn;

hints: Use id - rn as the grouping key.
